newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan MOF says reprimands its inspectors of DKB.
newsitem.headline: Japan MOF says reprimands its inspectors of DKB.

text.p: Japan's Ministry of Finance (MOF) said in a statement on Tuesday that it had reprimanded ministry officials who conducted inspections of scandal-tainted Dai-Ichi Kangyo Bank Ltd for "acts that could invite suspicions".
A MOF official told reporters that two ministry officials assigned to inspect DKB in 1994 had been entertained with food and drinks by DKB officials and had also played golf with them.
He said the expenses for the entertainment had been paid by the bank.
The two officials had taken steps on Tuesday to reimburse DKB for the expenses, he said. He did not say how much money was involved.
Current Vice Finance Minister Takeshi Komura also received a written warning from the ministry as he headed the minister's secretariat at the time, the official said.
In that post Komura was partly responsible for overseeing the conduct of ministry officials.

The ministry said in a statement that although it was important to exchange information with financial institutions under inspection it was necessary to maintain discipline so that inspections would not lose social credibility.
The MOF official said the acts had not affected the results of the inspection.
He declined to disclose the names of DKB officials involved but said one was one of four former bankers the ministry filed a complaint against with prosecutors on Friday.
The complaint alleged they had hidden information about problem loans to a "sokaiya" racketeer during the ministry inspection in 1994.
